summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of DSP Pension Fund within the NPS framework, including tax benefits and investment options, but contains some outdated information regarding the frequency of changing asset allocation.

claims.claim: NPS offers tax benefits under Sections 80C, 80CCD(1B), and 80CCD(2) of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: NPS contributions are eligible for tax deductions under these sections.

claims.claim: For non-government sector subscribers, the maximum allocation to Equity (E) is capped at 75% till age 50, gradually reducing thereafter.
claims.note: While 75% equity was the cap under Active Choice, the Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) introduced in October 2025 allows for up to 100% equity allocation for non-government subscribers in specific high-risk schemes.

claims.claim: The PFRDA regularly publishes performance data of all PFMs, which can be accessed on the NPS Trust website.
claims.note: Both NPS Trust and PFRDA websites provide performance data for PFMs.

claims.claim: If you are on Active Choice and your asset allocation has drifted significantly from your target, consider initiating a rebalance. Remember, you can modify your asset allocation twice in a financial year.
claims.note: NPS subscribers can change their asset allocation up to four times in a financial year, not twice.

claims.claim: If, after thorough review, you decide to switch your PFM, understand the online process for changing your Pension Fund Manager through the CRA portal. You can change your PFM once in a financial year.
claims.note: Subscribers are allowed to change their PFM once per financial year.

claims.claim: The fees for Pension Fund Managers in NPS are regulated by the PFRDA and are generally very low. They include an investment management fee, which is a small percentage of assets under management, and other transaction charges.
claims.note: PFRDA regulates NPS fees, including investment management fees, which are indeed a small percentage of AUM.
